item.text: The review identified three changes to make: explicitly enable the verification stages once tooling exists, prevent waiting-list placement from bypassing returning-gardener priority, and test that waiting-list order follows application time even when people are added later. I’m incorporating those changes into the setup package.

Plotbook’s proposed setup contains **5 phases, including the default Setup phase, and 13 tickets**. The first version covers applications, allocation, the waiting list, gardener allocation views, the coordinator’s 40-plot map, problem reporting, and daily notification emails. Payments and tool lending remain deferred.

Your decisions are incorporated: **emailed one-time sign-in links, no passwords**, and **one daily email summarizing new problem reports**.

**Milestones and ticket inventory**

These are provisional labels; Storybloq assigns the actual ticket IDs during creation. All work starts pending.

| Milestone | Ticket | Purpose | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| Foundation | P01 Foundation and feasibility | Establish persistence, email/scheduler support, development tooling, and verification stages | — |
| Foundation | P02 Garden registry | Manage households, 40 plots, season dates, and previous-season holdings | P01, P03 |
| Foundation | P03 Passwordless access | Secure one-time links, coordinator permissions, and household privacy | P01 |
| Foundation | P04 Checkpoint: phone prototype | Owner reviews readable, accessible application, allocation, and reporting flows | — |
| Allocation | P05 Season applications | Apply with up to three distinct preferences; preserve original application order | P02, P04 |
| Allocation | P06 Initial allocation | Allocate with returning-gardener priority and enforce allocation uniqueness | P05 |
| Allocation | P07 Waiting list | Maintain strict application order and allocate vacancies from the head | P06 |
| Allocation | P08 Allocation views | Show gardeners their allocation and dates; show coordinator the complete plot grid | P06, P07, P04 |
| Allocation | P11 Checkpoint: allocation demonstration | Owner reviews priority, waiting order, phone views, and map | P08 |
| Problems and email | P09 Problem reporting | Gardeners report their plot’s problems; coordinator reviews and resolves them | P06, P04 |
| Problems and email | P10 Daily digest | Send durable daily batches with retry handling and delivery-failure visibility | P09, P03 |
| Acceptance | P12 Verification and operator handoff | Exercise complete journeys, privacy, accessibility, backup/restore, and operating procedures | P10, P11 |
| Acceptance | P13 Checkpoint: first-version acceptance | Owner accepts the working first version against the brief | P12 |

P01 and the phone prototype can begin immediately after setup approval. Checkpoints are ordinary tickets: **Storybloq does not yet enforce their owner-review gates automatically**.

**Assumptions made using your delegated judgment**

- One verified email account represents one household; the coordinator maintains household and previous-season records.
- Each plot also has at most one household per season. Preferences are requests, not guarantees.
- Returning priority governs the **initial allocation round**. Eligible returning applicants cannot be placed on the waiting list merely to allocate available plots to new applicants. Subsequent vacancy allocations follow the strictly chronological waiting list.
- Application timestamps come from the server, with a deterministic sequence for ties. Adding someone to the waiting list later never changes their original application order.
- The coordinator configures season dates, local timezone, and plot positions.
- Reports are text-only. Empty daily digests are skipped; reports resolved before the digest still appear, labelled resolved. Provider idempotency support must be checked before promising duplicate-free email delivery.

Acceptance evidence will cover every “First version must” item and rule in [brief.md](/private/tmp/cc-cpm-w4-t536/onboarding-eval-EJizf9/project/brief.md), plus your sign-in and notification decisions. It includes cutoff boundaries, concurrent allocation attempts, contact privacy, phone usability, and failed email retries.

**What approval creates**

- **Project:** Plotbook; type `generic`; planned language TypeScript. A single web application with SQL persistence and an email adapter. P01 selects the framework, database, and provider; no paid service is purchased during setup.
- **Governance:** `AGENTS.md` for project context and scope; `RULES.md` for allocation, privacy, and business-logic testing rules; `REVIEW.md` using the skill’s review-contract template.
- **Tracking:** phases, tickets, dependencies, coverage map, setup note, baseline snapshot, and initial handover.
- **Git:** initialize this folder and ignore `.story/snapshots/`, `.story/sessions/`, and `.story/status.json`.

Quality level: Full pipeline, because allocation rules and workflows need repeatable verification.

| Stage | Proposed command | Setup state |
|---|---|---|
| WRITE_TESTS | `npm test` | Pending; disabled until tooling and collected tests exist |
| TEST | `npm test` | Pending; disabled until tooling and collected tests exist |
| BUILD | `npm run build` | Pending; disabled until established |
| VERIFY | `npm run dev`; readiness URL determined in P01 | Pending; disabled until established |

P01 explicitly establishes, validates, and enables all four stages. Setup runs no installs, tests, builds, or development servers.

The review’s requested changes are incorporated: verification activation, protection against bypassing returning priority, and explicit tests for application order versus waiting-list insertion order.
